text.headline: Timeline of Croatia
text.text: Major events in the history of Croatia.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The area of present-day Croatia has been inhabited since the Neolithic period, with evidence of early agricultural communities. These settlements laid the foundation for future civilizations in the region.

events.headline: Illyrian Tribes
events.text: By the first millennium BC, the Illyrians, a group of tribes, inhabited the western Balkans, including modern Croatia. They played a significant role in the region's early history and culture.

events.headline: Roman Conquest
events.text: The Romans conquered the Illyrian territories, integrating them into the Roman Empire. This led to the establishment of cities such as Pula and Split, which remain significant today.

events.headline: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: The Western Roman Empire fell, leading to the rise of various barbarian kingdoms in the region, including the Ostrogoths and later the Byzantines. This marked a significant shift in power dynamics in the area.

events.headline: Formation of the Kingdom of Croatia
events.text: Tomislav became the first king of Croatia, uniting various tribes and establishing the Kingdom of Croatia. This marked the beginning of a distinct Croatian state.

events.headline: Pacta Conventa
events.text: The Pacta Conventa was an agreement that established a personal union between the Kingdom of Croatia and the Kingdom of Hungary. This arrangement influenced Croatian politics for centuries.

events.headline: Battle of Mohács
events.text: The defeat of the Hungarian army at the Battle of Mohács led to the Habsburgs gaining control over Croatia. This marked the beginning of a long period of Habsburg influence in the region.

events.headline: Croatian National Revival
events.text: The Croatian National Revival, or Illyrian Movement, sought to promote Croatian language and culture. This period was crucial for the development of Croatian national identity.

events.headline: End of World War I
events.text: Following the end of World War I, Croatia became part of the newly formed Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes, later known as Yugoslavia. This marked a significant political change for Croatia.

events.headline: Nazi Occupation
events.text: During World War II, Croatia was occupied by Axis forces and became a puppet state under the Ustaše regime. This period was marked by severe repression and conflict.

events.headline: Post-War Yugoslavia
events.text: After World War II, Croatia became a republic within the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This period saw significant industrialization and social changes.

events.headline: Independence Declaration
events.text: Croatia declared independence from Yugoslavia on June 25, 1991, following a referendum. This marked the beginning of the Croatian War of Independence.

events.headline: Operation Storm
events.text: Operation Storm was a military operation that led to the liberation of Croatian territory occupied by Serb forces. This operation was a turning point in the Croatian War of Independence.

events.headline: Reintegration of Eastern Slavonia
events.text: Eastern Slavonia was reintegrated into Croatia after a peaceful transition, marking the end of the Croatian War of Independence. This event was significant for national reconciliation.

events.headline: EU Membership
events.text: Croatia officially became a member of the European Union on July 1, 2013. This marked a significant milestone in Croatia's post-war development and integration into Europe.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic affected Croatia significantly, leading to health and economic challenges. The government implemented various measures to combat the spread of the virus.

events.headline: Eurozone Membership
events.text: Croatia adopted the euro as its official currency on January 1, 2023, becoming the 20th member of the Eurozone. This transition aimed to strengthen its economy and integration within Europe.
